claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. I'll need to ask you some questions to assess your situation.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have children. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to learn more about Alex's situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any kind of education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** If so, when did he leave education, and when did he register?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and is taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

One more important question: **Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me also confirm a few final details:

**When did Alex leave school/education?** (For example, was it recently, or has it been several months?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a few months ago, around the end of the summer term.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me, let me explain the situation:

**For Alex (age 17):**

Under UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 16. For children aged 16-19, you can continue to receive Child Benefit **only if** they stay in approved education or training.

There is an exception: you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

In Alex's case:
- He is 17 years old
- He left education a few months ago (end of summer term)
- He is not in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a careers service or the armed services
- He is not working

Since Alex is not in approved education or training and has not registered with a careers service or armed services, he does not meet the criteria for Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16.

However, please note that if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he registered. This would need to be done while he is still 17.

If Alex returns to approved education or training in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point, as long as he is still under 20 years old.
